description:
PR #1332 fixed Windows CRLF trailing-delimiter misdetection by routing benchbox/core/data_organization/sorting.py::_source_has_trailing_delimiter through the shared helper benchbox/utils/file_format.py::has_trailing_delimiter. The fix is correct, but it is correct for an IMPLICIT reason: has_trailing_delimiter reads via _check_first_nonempty_line, which opens 'rt' (and mode='rt' for the compressed branch), so Python universal-newlines translates 
 to 
 before either checker runs. Both checkers then rstrip('
') only. Nothing pins that. If any read path is ever switched to binary for throughput - plausible for multi-GB TBL files - CRLF stops being normalized, the field count or the ends-with check shifts, and the original Windows bug returns silently. Second, narrower point: the merged CRLF tests only feed trailing-delimiter input. _write_tbl_crlf() has no clean variant, so of the four cells in (LF|CRLF) x (clean|trailing-delimiter), only clean-CRLF is unexercised end-to-end. Note the LF clean case IS covered by test_reads_normalized_tbl_with_no_trailing_delimiter, so a checker hardcoded to True would already be caught - this is coverage symmetry and invariant pinning, not a live defect. Also note has_trailing_delimiter's column_names=None fallback (ends-with check) is reachable but unused by all 10 platform callers, which all pass column names; it deserves the same CRLF assertion.

work_units.evidence: Added TestHasTrailingDelimiterFraming to tests/unit/utils/test_file_format.py - has_trailing_delimiter had NO direct unit test before this; the only coverage was indirect, via three platform test files. Pins all four framing/terminator cells (CRLF+trailing True, CRLF+clean False, LF+trailing True, LF+clean False) against BOTH checkers: the column_names field-count path that all ten platform callers use, and the column_names=None ends-with fallback, which is reachable but taken by no current caller. Plus a realistic multi-row CRLF file and a file with leading blank CRLF lines. Fixtures are explicit bytes so CRLF is exercised on every platform, not only the Windows nightly leg. 10 tests, all passing.
work_units.summary: Add the four-cell has_trailing_delimiter unit test, including the column_names=None fallback

work_units.evidence: Gave _write_tbl_crlf a trailing_delimiter flag (default True, so the two existing callers are unchanged) and added test_reads_clean_tbl_with_crlf_line_endings - the fourth cell of the writer's matrix. It asserts the output schema is exactly ['id','l_shipdate'], i.e. no synthetic trailing column survives on input that has none. Honest note on what this case does and does not catch: under a simulated binary-read regression it PASSES, because a failed probe returns False and clean input needs no synthetic column. It guards the opposite direction - a probe that wrongly reports a trailing delimiter would add a column to an N-field file and fail here. The trailing-delimiter cases catch false negatives; this catches false positives. Together they pin both.
work_units.summary: Give _write_tbl_crlf a trailing_delimiter flag and cover clean-CRLF end to end in the writer

work_units.evidence: Stated the requirement where it lives, in _check_first_nonempty_line's docstring: TEXT MODE IS REQUIRED, NOT INCIDENTAL, with the causal chain spelled out - both reads open 'rt', universal newlines translate CRLF to LF before the checker, and every checker strips only backslash-n, so a binary read leaves a stray CR that adds a phantom field, breaks the ends-with match, and on bytes makes rstrip raise, which the blanket except turns into a confident 'no trailing delimiter'. Points at the test that enforces it. The enforcement is behavioural, not a source grep: simulating the regression by switching the uncompressed read to 'rb' fails 6 of the 10 framing tests and 2 of the 3 writer CRLF tests. Verified and reverted; file restored byte-for-byte.
work_units.summary: Pin the text-mode requirement in the helper so a binary-read change has to confront it
